items.title: Elden Ring Guide Hub
items.summary: Our Elden Ring guide hub covers the base game and Shadow of the Erdtree, including bosses, weapons, quests, Spirit Ashes, items, puzzles, and more.
items.content:
Elden Ring is a massive game filled with difficult bosses, hidden locations, character questlines, powerful weapons, rare items, and more than a few mechanics that FromSoftware doesn’t fully explain. Even experienced Soulslike players can find themselves wondering where to go or what they’re supposed to do next.

That’s why we’ve put together this Elden Ring guide hub. Here you’ll find all of our guides for the original game and the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion, covering everything from Spirit Ashes and character progression to weapons, spells, puzzles, boss encounters, and hard-to-find locations.

We’ll continue updating this page whenever we publish additional Elden Ring guides and coverage.

FromSoftware took everything it learned from Demon’s Souls , Dark Souls , Bloodborne , and Sekiro and placed it inside a massive open world. Our original review breaks down the combat, exploration, bosses, progression, PC performance, and everything else that helped make Elden Ring one of FromSoftware’s most ambitious games.

The Land of Shadow introduces an enormous new region filled with layered exploration, dangerous enemies, memorable boss encounters, and plenty of secrets. Our review explains why Shadow of the Erdtree was worth the wait and how it expands upon the original Elden Ring experience.

Wondering how much time you’ll need to explore the Land of Shadow? This guide breaks down how long it takes to complete the main story and how your playtime can change depending on your skill level and how much optional content you tackle.

The Cerulean Coast can be surprisingly difficult to reach if you don’t know which path to follow. We’ll guide you from the Castle Front Site of Grace, through the Ellac River, and into one of the most visually striking areas in the expansion.

Ancient Dragon-Man stands between you and the path leading toward Jagged Peak and Charo’s Hidden Grave. This guide covers the encounter, his attacks, how to prepare for the fight, and what you’ll receive for defeating him.

Having trouble finding the location depicted in the Domains of Dragons painting? We’ll show you how to reach the correct spot on Jagged Peak and claim the Rock Heart, which allows your character to transform into a dragon.

The Star-Lined Sword is a unique katana designed for players using Dexterity, Strength, and Intelligence. Here’s where to find Demi-Human Queen Marigga and how to defeat her to claim the weapon.

Getting the Sword of Light requires more than simply finding it inside a chest. You’ll first need to obtain the Stone-Sheathed Sword before taking it to the correct altar and transforming it into this powerful Holy weapon.

Magic users looking to expand their collection of gravity sorceries will want to track down the Gravitational Missile. We’ll show you where to find the returning Fallingstar Beast in Scaduview and how to earn the spell.

The Blessing of Marika completely restores your HP, removes status ailments, and is extremely rare. This guide shows you the three locations where we found this valuable consumable in the Land of Shadow.

Used all of the Walking Mausoleums in the original game? Shadow of the Erdtree includes three additional locations where you can duplicate Remembrances without needing another mausoleum.

items.title: The Duskbloods isn't just 'Nintendo Bloodborne', it's better than Elden Ring: Nightreign
items.summary: It doesn't deserve the hate it's been getting.
items.content:
The Duskbloods is a solid multiplayer experience and proof FromSoftware can do more than just traditional soulsborne.

FromSoftware’s Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive, The Duskbloods , recently finally invited players to see what it’s all about - and despite some initial technical hiccups, I actually quite enjoyed it.

Before I dive into my thoughts and feelings, I can confidently say that my time with The Duskbloods was more enjoyable than Elden Ring: Nightreign . That’s not to say I don’t like Nightreign , but aside from the odd game with friends, it never gave me much of a reason to stick around.

The Duskbloods felt different however. Once the server issues were mended and players could finally jump into some matches, it was clear this is more than FromSoftware trying to relive its Bloodborne glory days.

You’ll no doubt have seen some of the memes online, but when it came time to select a character, I felt compelled to choose Zork.

This goofy little guy perfectly exemplifies why The Duskbloods is a completely different animal to any other FromSoftware game.

Each character has their own unique design, fighting style, special abilities and general stat loadout. As a strength build aficionado, Zork looked like the right choice for me and boy oh boy was I correct.

Aside from his heavy weapon and bulky armour, Zork’s ability lets him ascend into the air and become a living missile directed at anything you’re locked on to.

I let out a hearty chuckle every time I chased down a fleeing player with this move, and even when I went off course and paid the price, it was still a good laugh. His other move is a missile barrage, which was great for pummelling enemies at range.

Once you’re accustomed to what your character can do, your objective is to kill. Like Elden Ring: Nightreign , slaying enemies gradually levels you up, but what I love about The Duskbloods is there’s no penalty for biting off more than you can chew. If you die, your level remains the same, meaning you can spawn back in and have another go, or wander off in search of easier prey.

Sigils are scattered throughout the map hiding powerful NPC allies, which you can summon like eldritch Pokémon to help you overpower foes, or just draw their attention while you heal up from afar. Again, this gave me a good laugh, especially one that sang opera before giving an unsuspected enemy the prime Hoarah Loux experience (just straight hands and elbow drops).

The ultimate goal is to raise your level as high as possible within the time-limit, as the players with the lowest rank get eliminated from the game.

Those fortunate or skilled enough to make it to the end take part in one final battle against your fellow survivors, for the ultimate glory.

In essence, that’s what I loved most about The Duskbloods, and it completely rid me of my woes over the game being PvPvE.

items.title: The Duskbloods Playtest Was Even More Popular Than Elden Ring Nightreign’s
The Duskbloods Network Test Surpassed Elden Ring Nightreign in Applicants
items.summary: Despite its exclusivity to the Nintendo Switch 2, the first network test for The Duskbloods drew an impressive turnout.
items.content:
By Daniel Trock Published Aug 24, 2026, 2:57 PM EDT Daniel Trock is a Contributor at DualShockers specializing in PC games, lists, and reviews. He has been writing professionally since 2018 and covering games since 2020, with previous work spanning guides, news, lists, and reviews across multiple publications.

Before joining DualShockers, Daniel contributed guides to GamerJournalist and lists to TheGamer . He currently covers tech topics for SlashGear and BGR . He holds a Bachelor’s Degree in Psychology from Marist College and a Master of Fine Arts in Creative and Professional Writing from Western Connecticut State University .

on Google Preferred Source Google News Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap In this day and age, I guess it really shouldn’t be especially surprising that a new game from FromSoftware is a hot-button topic. Even back when Elden Ring Nightreign was announced and people were skeptical about its pseudo-battle royale multiplayer format, it didn’t stop an outpouring of applicants for the game’s initial test runs last year, nor its success at full launch.

While FromSoft’s pedigree does carry a natural disposition toward success, there were factors against the recent network test for its newest multiplayer endeavor, The Duskbloods , chief among them being its exclusivity to the Nintendo Switch 2.

Every Soulsborne fan is going through some serious déjà vu as Hidetaka Miyazaki sets sight on directing an exclusive for the Switch 2: The Duskbloods.

However, it seems that once again, nothing can stand in FromSoft’s way, because as its staff tells it, not only was the first network test for The Duskbloods a rousing success, it actually managed to draw more applicants than Elden Ring Nightreign did.

Whether or not that’s proof positive that the game will be another slam dunk remains to be seen, but if nothing else, it’s clear that the obstacle of platform exclusivity is no obstacle at all to fans of Soulslikes. Either that, or the initial announcement that The Duskbloods would be Switch 2-exclusive got a lot of people to buy the console.

In an August 22 livestream hosted by Famitsu , later translated by GamesRadar , FromSoftware producer Yasuhiro Kitao spoke about the overwhelming response from the playing public to the Duskbloods network test that ran from August 21 to August 24. As Kitao tells it, the first network test for The Duskbloods drew in even more applicants than those who applied to the network tests for Elden Ring Nightrein in May 2025.

“We were really surprised,” Kitao said during the stream. Kitao didn’t provide any hard numbers for the number of applicants for the Duskbloods network test, nor are there any player counts available for the Nightreign tests, though Bandai Namco did release a little infographic after the Nightreign test with some miscellaneous stats like the number of runes lost and the number of times players summoned Spectral Hawks.

FromSoftware has finally announced the release date for The Duskbloods' Network Test, giving fans their first chance to experience its gameplay.

What’s especially surprising about this revelation is that, where both Nightreign and its network test were full multi-platform affairs, available on PC, Xbox One, Xbox Series X/S, PS4, and PS5, the Duskbloods is steadfastly exclusive to the Switch 2. For The Duskbloods’ test to outpace applicants across five platforms, needless to say, it was quite the high-profile affair.

With the network test for The Duskbloods done and dusted, the only remaining mystery for the game is when players will actually get their hands on it. As far as anyone knows, the game is still slated to meet its 2026 release window, with an alleged leak claiming that the game is planned to launch on September 24 , exacerbating an already exceptionally cramped month of high-profile gaming with the looming launches of games like Onimusha: Way of the Sword, Marvel’s Wolverine, and Control Resonant.

That said, the network test wasn’t without its foibles. The beginning of the proceedings was particularly fraught , as players couldn’t even get past the initial log-in screen and into the game proper. These issues seemed to be gradually ironed out as the testing period went on, and as of now, the vibe toward the game does seem to be veering positive. If that leaked release date is legit, FromSoft has exactly one month to get things up to snuff before we see just how well a Switch 2-exclusive multiplayer Soulslike game can really stand up to its contemporaries.

items.title: It Wasn't Fun To Lose In The Duskbloods Network Test
items.summary: What if someone just irredeemably sucks at PvP?
items.content:
After putting well over a hundred hours into Elden Ring Nightreign , I have been stoked out of my mind for The Duskbloods . Even though I had never engaged in FromSoftware PvP before, the PvE aspects of The Duskbloods really appealed to me, and all the previews suggested that the game itself would include enough of a balance of both that I could get by being somewhat mediocre at murdering other players…at least until the final clash. I braced myself: I was probably going to lose a lot, and that was fine. I was going to have fun!

Well, the network test is over now, and I had…some fun, I guess. I also had a pretty bad time, because I lost. A lot. Like, egregiously. And losing was deeply unfun. And I’m struggling to work out in my head if things will be better in the actual game, or if I’m just doomed to suck at The Duskbloods and should give up and go back to Nightreign .

Now, not all my frustration is loss-related. I actually came out of the weekend with the firm conviction that a Network Test is a terrible environment in which to preview a game. For one, I couldn’t play with my friends. I usually play Nightreign in trios with my partner and a good friend. We know that The Duskbloods is only going to be set up for singles and duos, but we were hoping we’d at least be able to all queue into the same game together and compete with each other. I genuinely have no idea if I’ll be able to do that in the final game or not, though, because that feature was unavailable in the Network Test. We did occasionally manage to get into the same games together by queuing at the exact same time and forming alliances when we could. Those moments where we could team up and work together to collect virtue, defend against other players, and take on bosses were some of the best during all my sessions. But it sucked to not be able to consistently share my experience with my friends, and I hope the main game includes that option.

Additionally, the Network Test only had one map available, and a selection of six characters. It took me a while to click with a character, but by the end I ended up liking Trang Lanh quite a bit when I could pair her with a Kin (an NPC ally) that could tank or distract for me a bit. The test also had what I suspect was a deliberately limited pool of bosses and enemies and events. I don’t know that the main game will have more of the latter (it will have three maps and ten characters to start), but if all those options aren’t expanded, it’s going to get real boring, real fast. After a few hours of play, every match felt painfully similar, which I think made losing repeatedly feel even worse than it would have otherwise.

Comment by u/Jam_beter_then_jelly from discussion in TheDuskbloods

Now look. I’m not a sore loser. I suck at all sorts of games and still have fun with them. And I’m extremely willing to admit that PvP is not my bag. But I guess I just thought I’d stand a little more of a chance than I did. The trailers and previews really made it seem like players who wanted to focus more on PvE could use boss fights and exploration to buff themselves up enough to hold their own when it was time to fight. And I think that might be true, but the problem is I kept getting murdered by other players while trying to do these other activities. Folks just swooped in on me and took me out, again and again, then stole my kill or flame or whatever for themselves. On one hand, preventing me from getting virtue and getting some of your own is a viable strategy, I guess. On the other hand, there’s no real reward for killing other players outside of Ritual Sites and certain Sigils (basically specific goals you might have within a match), so getting demolished repeatedly just felt…bad. One guy even killed me, then immediately teleported to the same place I spawned back at, and killed me again before I could get my head on straight. Why!

Also, you have to get really close to people to form Alliances with them, but if you get close your Kin likes to attack unprompted, which often led people to think I was attacking them, which prompted them to attack me while I was menuing and…yeah.

There are demons playing this game by u/kao24429774 in TheDuskbloods

Also , it seemed like so much comes down to those Ritual Sites, zones players are directed to with goals like claiming stones, defending a pledge, or killing other players, such that the end of every phase 2 and 3 was essentially a PvP free-for-all. If I wanted to instead spend that time taking down a Trespasser boss or something, I could, but I’d be doing it alone because everyone else was busy at war in the chapel or clock tower or something. Usually by this time I was desperate enough to try a Ritual Site, but again, I suck at PvP, so I just died. Again and again. After playing for almost ten hours over the weekend, I didn’t make it to the final Grail fight once. The highest high I felt was the one time I managed to defeat my “sworn enemy,” selected for me by my Sigil before he could kill me…only to prompt him to spend the rest of the match hunting me down and killing me over and over and over again. Exciting stuff.

I do want to be clear that I also liked a lot of elements of The Duskbloods . The movement is super fun: I love the quadruple jumps and holy hell that air dash is sick. I love ripping into enemies as the Senator in his dinosaur form, or unleashing a hell of bullets on distant bosses with Layla. All the visual design elements are incredible, from the characters to the Trespasser bosses to the environment itself. I loved finding little hidden areas on the map, like the underground ruins or the top room of the clock tower. I love (most of) the Kin partners, especially the wolf that tears enemies up and the annoyingly persistent Marlowe (the Baritone, however, needs to shut the hell up). And I really, really want to like the premise here: a FromSoftware action game where multiple people are in the world at once, competing and cooperating in different ways simultaneously. That’s cool to me! I want to participate in that!

So, I feel torn. On one hand, this was just the Network Test! It wasn’t here for me to develop complete feelings on the game; it was here to test the networks and make sure they worked, which ( after the first session ) they largely did, very well. Still, it was a valid preview of (some of) what’s to come, provided to myself and other players presumably in the hopes we would enjoy it and want to buy the game. But I didn’t have much fun, and it’s just so hard to tell how much, if any, the vibe of The Duskbloods will change for me upon release. Apparently,you can still progress the story in the full game even if you lose repeatedly, and if that’s the case I might have a better time because at least I’ll feel I’m accomplishing something with each loss. It’s also possible there will be a character in the final roster that I will really click with. It’s also possible that the final game’s skill-based matchmaking will work in my favor more and put me with folks more on my level, or that the meta will develop in such a way as to encourage players to leave me alone while I explore during the first few phases so I’ll have a bit more of a fighting chance in the later ones. Or maybe I’ll just be able to queue with my friends, so even if I lose, I’ll still have fun running around with people I like. Or as the meta develops, maybe I’ll become more familiar with a strategy that will help me collect virtue while avoiding players. That’s a lot of maybes, though!

And it’s also possible that I just, with time, get good. At the moment, I don’t see any world in which I can close the massive skill gap between myself and folks who have been doing this sort of thing for years, but who knows? It’s just, in order to improve, I have to be motivated to play. Losing in a game like this still has to be at least a little fun, or else people like me drop out over time, the skill ceiling keeps rising, and the game gets super sweaty. Is losing over and over at The Duskbloods fun enough to motivate me to improve? In the Network Test, it was unfortunately not. In the main game, it might be. I’m still going to try The Duskbloods out at launch, but the excitement I felt at the prospect of vampire battle royale going into the weekend has had a lot of blood drained out of it.

items.title: The Duskbloods is Comparable to Elden Ring, Bloodborne “In Terms of Sheer Volume,” Says Director
items.summary: Hidetaka Miyzaki has also confirmed that players will have plenty of customization options for their loadouts in the full game.
items.content:
Having kicked off the network test for The Duskbloods , developer FromSoftware has revealed details about what players can expect from the PvPvE title when it finally comes out. Speaking to VideoGamesChronicle , director Hidetaka Miyazaki said that the full release of The Duskbloods will give players more options when it comes to customizing their loadouts. This was a big question, since the network test only offers preset loadouts.

“You have to customize your Bloodsworn with which weapons and skills they hold and take into each match. One of these customization elements is actually which event you prefer. So which event you want to see come up more, and one of these events could be the final phase being a boss battle rather than a three-way match, something like this.

“So, these player tendencies. This is one area that the matchmaking will be looking at and trying to pool players of like mind together.”

Miyzaki also noted that the amount of content in The Duskbloods will be comparable to what we’ve previously seen with games like Elden Ring and Bloodborne , especially when it comes to worldbuilding and lore. Acknowledging the fact that the network test only has a few lore elements, he said that the team is excited to see players experience the full story when the title comes out.

“In the network test, there’s not a lot of these lore elements. But it’s something that we’re concentrating on for the full release, and we look forward to players discovering a lot about these different characters. They’ve all been prepared with their own backgrounds, their own personalities and settings, and there’s a lot of relationships between the Bloodsworn and their blood families, their blood ties. We hope players will pick up more on these histories and these backgrounds of the characters as they play.

“In terms of sheer volume of text and lore to dig through, I feel like it compares to our titles up until now. So, I think there’ll be, as you unlock more about these characters and you uncover more of their narratives, there’s going to be a lot of a lot to dig through and enjoy there, and discover the connections between the Bloodsworn and their histories.”

In terms of just gameplay, The Duskbloods is slated to launch with a single map, with two more coming later. Out of the ten planned characters, six will be available on day one. FromSoftware hasn’t offered much in the way of a roadmap for when this content will make its way into the game. However, this should come as no surprise since The Duskbloods also doesn’t have a release date yet.

The Duskbloods is being developed exclusively for the Nintendo Switch 2. While some FromSoftware fans might be worried about the title’s PvPvE gameplay structure, Miyazaki has said that players don’t necessarily have to be good at PvP in order to enjoy the game. To achieve this, he discussed developing gameplay systems that would appeal to him despite his lack of interest in engaging in PvP games.

items.title: Winning a match of The Duskbloods on Switch 2 got my blood pumping –but, wow, what a weird game it is
items.summary: It's like someone gave Nightreign some Night Nurse (in a good way)
items.content:
Gaming Winning a match of The Duskbloods on Switch 2 got my blood pumping –but, wow, what a weird game it is T3 Follow Max Freeman-Mills Mon, August 24, 2026 at 3:00 PM UTC Add us on Google Mon, August 24, 2026 at 3:00 PM UTC When you buy through links on our articles, Future and its syndication partners may earn a commission.

Whether you call a network test a beta, a demo, or just a network test, it's generally the first opportunity that most of us get to go hands-on with a FromSoftware game, making it a thrilling moment. The Duskbloods has been a mysterious concept for well over a year at this point, but this past weekend I was able to play it for a couple of hours to see what it actually involves.

A Switch 2 exclusive from FromSoftware is always going to be an eye-catching prospect, but I didn't expect the game to begin with quite such a cinematic introduction. In fact, it opens much like a single-player game from the studio, with an enigmatic cut-scene, and a journey through some very scenic areas before a boss who'll likely kill you.

Before long, you'll have the controls down, but you'll need to complete at least a few more tuturials before you understand what the game actually is . The answer? It's a lot like Elden Ring: Nightreign , but way slower and more digestible.

A match of The Duskbloods starts with you selecting an area of the map to spawn into, at the same time as seven other players. Over the course of three rounds, you'll explore that map, killing enemies to level up, but also completing objectives that accumulate a currency called Virtue.

At the end of each round, the players with the least Virtue will be culled, and the game ends with the top three players fighting in a small PvP arena, each with two lives. That's the broad strokes of the game, but there's a lot to learn as you explore. There are a bunch of ways to gain Virtue, for instance.

Some players will naturally gravitate towards basically hunting down their rivals, and this can be profitable. Thankfully, death doesn't set you back too far, since you respawn quickly with no lost progress – your loss is more in the form of others' gain.

If you want, though, you can largely play the game as if the other players are just high-level enemies you want to avoid. My first match, for instance, saw me doing just that, simply exploring the map and killing high-value enemies to eventually enter the final battle with more Virtue than anyone else despite never having killed a human enemy.

I won that battle, largely by having something resembling a brain and just holding off while the other two players ground each other's health pools down. I can't pretend it wasn't thrilling, though, and it was also pretty funny to take a photo of the post-match screen with its series of confusing tallies – breaking down where I got my Virtue with symbols that I still don't understand.

While exploring the map, you can find Kin, which are basically summons that you can level up if you concentrate on it. They're hugely helpful in both PvE and PvP, and I found at least three different ones to experiment with. That's one layer of build-craft, with another being the character you choose to play as. This test had four, but there will apparently be more than a dozen at launch.

This is a huge differentiator from Nightreign . There's no scrambling to find good weapons, since your base attacks and even your magic powers are determined by your character pick. Instead, the main variable is how far you manage to level up, what Kin y you use, and whether you can earn some upgrades to branch out your stats and resistances.

The reality is, though, that with only a few hours of in-game time under my belt (largely thanks to the network test's very precise windows), I still feel like there's a huge amount to learn.

What I can say is that I thought the game ran well and looked lovely, though I only played it in docked mode since I was at home. It's targeting a frame rate of 60fps, which is key for smoothness, and while I saw some stutters, given it's not yet out, I'm pretty happy with performance.

Elden Ring hits Switch 2 this very week, and I think that game's far larger map and open areas could be more of a challenge for the hardware, but either way I'm thrilled to get major FromSoftware games on Switch 2 at all.

items.title: Magic: The Gathering 2027 Universes Beyond Predictions — Games of Thrones, Elden Ring, and More
items.summary: Following Hasbro's tease of more "fantasy-adjacent" Magic: The Gathering Universes Beyond sets for 2027, here are our predictions for what could join the lineup next year.
items.content:
Magic: The Gathering’s 2027 lineup is taking shape, with half of the six sets revealed. From a return to Kamigawa to afrofantasy and underwater adventures, we’re just waiting for our first look at Universes Beyond sets to fill out the calendar.

We’ll likely get our first look at MagicCon Atlanta in November, but for now, there’s no harm in some fun predictions on what could be coming up next.

In a recent quarterly earnings report , Hasbro CEO Chris Cocks noted feedback on recent Universes Beyond sets, which have run the gamut from two trips to Middle-Earth, just as many visits to New York City, every single Final Fantasy, and, soon, Star Trek.

“The one thing I'll say on the Universes Beyond partners that we have next year is they'll probably be a bit more fantasy-adjacent," he explained.

"And I don't think any of them will take place in New York City because we definitely have gotten that feedback from some fans."

We know there will be three new Universes Beyond sets, with one in April, one in August, and one in November. So, there are a lot of potential crossovers that would be fun for Magic: The Gathering, but the idea of refocusing on fantasy IP certainly is interesting.

Here are some that make some sense, all of which you can consider part of our Universes Beyond wishlist for 2027. Let's take a look.

Ooo boy, this would be big. Hasbro has already partnered with Nintendo to make The Legend of Zelda toys , but could that extend to Magic, too?

The core identity of a grand, fantasy adventure is a great fit, and the Final Fantasy set showed that Magic can take an IP that covers multiple stories, realities, and timelines and do each justice.

A Master Sword you can equip to Link, Bokoblin creatures to amass, and multiple powerful versions of Ganon make this an obvious fit. We've got the live-action Zelda film coming up soon as well, so this could be another big move for the series... if Nintendo allows it.

Sticking with fantasy video games, albeit much dirtier, grim, and morally gray ones, The Witcher series will return in the coming years with a fourth entry . There’s an absolute ton to pull from already, and Wizards of the Coast could even pick from the book series as well if its so inclined.

The main cast of characters would be easy to build a focus around, but there’s also such a deep bestiary that you can then add the griffin, the leshen, and much, much more. Saga cards based on iconic quests like The Bloody Baron would also be a fun way to relive some of Geralt’s most famous adventures.

Let's not forget that CD Projekt Red has also already dabbled in the card game space with Gwent: The Witcher Card Game , so there's also a bunch of fun concepts Wizards could riff from, and plenty of brilliant artists to call upon again if needed.

Yes, OK, it’s hardly swords and sorcery, but we know more Marvel sets are coming, so why not make it more about spellcraft than spandex, right?

Nightreign being multi-platform didn't give it the edge here

Between Elden Ring Nightreign's release last year and The Duskbloods coming this year, FromSoftware is truly in its multiplayer era right now. It's not that the studio is changing its trajectory to ditch single-player games , mind you, as boss Hidetaka Miyazaki says, "both of those ideas just coincided with being multiplayer games. It's not necessarily some big reveal saying that this is the direction we plan to go moving forward."

Perhaps, though, the success of last year's co-op, roguelike-flavored souls game left more folks excited to see what the studio was cooking up with The Duskbloods. In a livestream hosted by Famitsu (translated by GamesRadar+), FromSoftware producer Yasuhiro Kitao reveals that the number of applications for the Switch 2 game's closed network test exceeded that for Nightreign's. "We were really surprised," he notes.

It is surprising, given that the Switch 2 is a single platform – and one that only just launched last year – it's bound to have a smaller installed base than the combined force of PC, PS5, PS4, Xbox Series X|S, and Xbox One, as Nightreign has. Kitao acknowledges this, saying that FromSoftware questions if there really will be more Duskbloods players come launch, and noting that it'll probably be Nightreign that comes out on top.

Even so, it's a positive early sign for The Duskbloods. After all, multiplayer-focused games live and die by how many players they have – their popularity is usually what makes the difference between something being supported for years to come, or being quietly shelved.

FromSoftware knows what it's doing with The Duskbloods character Zork, the internet's new obsession: "I have developed a powerful, almost maternal affection."

items.content:

Many fans were surprised when FromSoftware announced its PvPvE action game, The Duskbloods, so soon after releasing its multiplayer, roguelike Elden Ring spin-off, Nightreign .

However, according to game director Miyazaki, who also helmed Elden Ring , Bloodborne , and Dark Souls , releasing two multiplayer games back-to-back wasn't intentional.

"It's funny because there was never really any big plan that these two games would both release next to each other," Miyazaki told IGN , explaining that since Nightreign was led by a different director, Junya Ishizaki, both ideas "just coincided with being multiplayer games."

"It's not necessarily some big reveal saying that this is the direction we plan to go moving forward," Miyazaki continued. "We still have a heavy focus on single-player content as well. This is just something that happened to work out the way it did."

Hold out for a little longer FromSoft fans — The Duskbloods will get a closed network test this summer, but a release date for the full game has yet to be announced The Duskbloods network test has finally revealed a few new details about FromSoftware's upcoming Switch 2 game, including multiplayer matches with 'up to eight players' 'Clair Obscur showed that you can take a genre and do it in a different and interesting way' — The Blood of Dawnwalker director says the ambitious game was made out of a 'love for RPGs' The director then suggested the studio could dive back into making single-player games after The Duskbloods arrives, saying: "But it's like, the more you work on something multiplayer for a long time, if anything, it scratches that itch only to want to make something single-player again."

The studio's last single-player experience was Elden Ring , which launched in 2022, followed by the multiplayer spin-off, Nighreign , in 2025.

Next up for FromSoftware is The Duskbloods , which was announced last year as a PvPvE and Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive. Network tests are underway, but a release date hasn't been set.

items.title: Rise with ELDEN RING Tarnished Edition, launching 28th August on Nintendo Switch 2
items.content:
The Lands Between—a place of myth, gods, and broken dreams. Long ago, Queen Marika and her divine offspring reigned here, but since the Elden Ring was shattered, the world has fallen into decay. Now, the land whispers for a King.

The ‘Tarnished’, long exiled, are finally seeing the light of Grace once more. Step into this hauntingly beautiful realm, unravel its ancient mysteries, and rise as the one true Elden Lord.

The ELDEN RING Tarnished Edition game arrives on the Nintendo Switch™ 2 system on 28th August .

The Lands Between are part of a vast continent, where magnificent open fields and huge dungeons with complex three-dimensional designs are seamlessly connected. As you explore, the joy of discovering unknown and overwhelming threats awaits you.

Mastery of the terrain and knowledge of its secrets can help you overcome enemies and defeat formidable bosses—or lead invading players into traps.

An epic drama born from a myth created by George R.R. Martin The founding mythology of Elden Ring was written by George R. R. Martin and adapted into a rich multilayered story. Intersecting goals and desires between the characters create an intense narrative that weaves throughout the Lands Between. The events of the game can unravel in many ways—depending on your interventions.

Combat is simple to learn yet offers hidden depths of dexterity. As you seek to become the Elden Lord, you’ll need to explore the balance between attacking, avoiding damage, using a wide variety of weapons, spells, summons, and perfecting your timing to take advantage of your opponents’ weaknesses.

Create and build your own character In addition to customising the appearance of your character, there are countless ways to combine the weapons, armour, usable items, and magic that you equip. You can develop your character according to your play style.

No matter if you prefer bold physical confrontation, tactical spellcasting, or the subtle art of stealth, you’ll be able to find gear that supports your choices.

Traverse together with other Nintendo Switch 2 players. You can play with up to two other Tarnished as your cooperative teammates, either by inviting them using a shared password or by summoning them from a pool of nearby community members.

There are also ample opportunities to face off against other players, either through co-op invasions, invited duels, or the many player battle options available in the three Colosseums.

If you’d like to learn more or begin your journey to the Lands Between by pre-ordering the Tarnished Edition, please check out the link below.

items.title: ELDEN RING - RAGING WOLF 1/6 SCALE STATUE
items.summary: Who is the Raging Wolf? Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to
items.content:
Who is the Raging Wolf?

Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to become the shadow of one of the Empyreans and built his strength relentlessly as he traveled through fallow Limgrave to the golden city of Leyndell. And yet in spite of all his strength, his armor is now worn by another… An unnamed Tarnished now walks the Lands Between in the skin of the wolf. Does this warrior seek the same fate as Vargram, forever stalking at the side of an Empyrean? Will they uphold the Golden Order or supplant it for some new code? Whatever the destination, woe befall upon any who dare block the path.

The most impressive Elden Ring statue yet

Standing at 33 cm/13 inches, it’s one of the largest character statues ever produced for ELDEN RING. Crafted with the attentive supervision of FromSoftware, this full 1/6 scale figure captures each minute detail with masterful skill. The size allows perfect fidelity to the beautiful and dark fantasy atmosphere of the game, including smears of bloody red across blade of the Bastard Sword and the crest of the Iron Roundshield. From the intricate filigrees of its helm to its whisps of silvered fur blown back by an errant breeze to the humble, dusty cloth wraps protecting the feet of its greaves against the mossy stones of the path to Stoneveil Castle, it’s a portrait of the implacable will of the Tarnished. All these expertly rendered touches from sculpturer Shinya Yamaoka make this statue a perfect match to the most iconic set from one of the most iconic games of this generation.

Where can I get a Raging Wolf Set statue?

Pre-orders for the Raging Wolf 1/6 scale statue can be placed on the official Bandai Namco website. At this time, based on the production estimates of Gecco studio, these stunning PVC/ABS figures will ship to your home in Winter of 2026. If you are a true aficionado of the game, there is no better purchase to bring the world of Elden Ring to your home or office. It’s a timeless piece for your own collection or an impressive gift for a friend or loved one. And one small note, if you have not yet found this set in the Lands Between for your Tarnished, we recommend you seek the aid of Recusant Bernahl at the Volcano Manor.

Place your order for the Raging Wolf statue on the official Bandai Namco Store.

*This product is available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.

items.title: ELDEN RING: SHADOW OF THE ERDTREE – Official Vinyl Soundtrack
items.summary: Follow in the foosteps of Miquella once more with this exclusive 2 disc vinyl collection, celebrating the sweeping, emotional journey of Shadow of the Erdtree. Presented with the reverence merited by a legendary expansion, this premium set
items.content:
Follow in the foosteps of Miquella once more with this exclusive 2 disc vinyl collection, celebrating the sweeping, emotional journey of Shadow of the Erdtree.

Presented with the reverence merited by a legendary expansion, this premium set is crafted for collectors, audiophiles, and Tarnished who seek to experience the Realm of Shadow through its music.

The Collection

Housed in a full color gatefold sleeve and marked with the symbol of Messmer the Impaler, each vinyl disc is pressed on heavyweight material to ensure optimal durability and warmth of playback. Whether displayed proudly on a shelf or played to relive your own quest, this set is designed as both a collector’s piece and a lasting tribute to one of the most celebrated expansions in modern gaming.

The Artists

Across 18 tracks, the soundtrack transforms the ELDEN RING experience into a powerful standalone odyssey—one carried by orchestral grandeur, ethereal choir work, and the signature melancholy that defines the worlds created by FromSoftware.

A Collector’s Treasure

This official vinyl set is an essential centerpiece for any discerning fan’s collection. Perfect for longtime followers of FromSoftware’s musical legacy or newcomers drawn into the Land of Shadow for the first time. *This vinyl is available exclusively on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, Middle East, India and the United States

items.title: Discover the ELDEN RING Blaidd The Half-Wolf Lamp
items.summary: Summon the legendary warrior into your world with the Blaidd The Half-Wolf Lamp, a handcrafted, LED-powered tribute to one of ELDEN RING ’s most iconic character. Designed for collectors, lore enthusiasts, and Tarnished alike, this unique n
items.content:
Summon the legendary warrior into your world with the Blaidd The Half-Wolf Lamp, a handcrafted, LED-powered tribute to one of ELDEN RING’s most iconic character.

Designed for collectors, lore enthusiasts, and Tarnished alike, this unique night lamp captures the tragic loyalty and silent strength of Blaidd, Shadow of Ranni.

The lamp features an LED-illuminated base that reveals glowing rune symbols beneath Blaidd’s feet, evoking the grace-given power that guides Tarnished across the Lands Between. Rising above it, an engraved acrylic summoning panel glows softly when lit, capturing the look and feel of an in-game summon sign and the spirit-calling magic it represents. Powered through a simple USB connection, it offers effortless illumination for any desk, gaming setup, or collector’s display.

"If ever thou shouldst call upon me… I shall come."

Blaidd’s oath echoes still. Now, he stands ready, not for battle, but as a silent guardian of your space.

Bring the moonlit magic of ELDEN RING into your world, one glowing rune at a time.

*This edition is available exclusively on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia and the United States.
